audit.whatIsWrong: Six of the seven chart rows disagree with their own explanations, and the whys are the ones that are right. whys[2] says 'the stage is even, not lost' but the row reads Swain. whys[3] says 'neither side decisively owns this window' — row reads Swain. whys[4] says this is 'the first stage where extended fights clearly favour you' — row reads Ziggs. whys[5] literally says 'Skill reflects the coin-flip nature' — row reads Swain. whys[6] says Ziggs reclaims the map — row reads Swain. The packet chart matches the whys exactly: Ziggs/Ziggs/Skill/Skill/Swain/Skill/Ziggs.
audit.why: The chart had been inverted against its own text at a 46.73% win rate, telling the reader they own the late game that every prose field on the page says they lose.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 set to the packet chart with ratings to match; every win[N] and phases[N].side proposed as a matched pair in one group.

audit.why: Four spikes present: his Levels 1-2 range advantage, your Level 6, your first item, and his late Mega Inferno Bomb siege. Mega Inferno Bomb is 120/95/70 s and 5000 range, which is exactly the late-game attrition the spike describes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is named in twelve places as the ability the entire lane is played around, but its cooldown appears nowhere. It is 20/18/16/14/12 — 20 s at rank 1. Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16 s at every rank, which the mid text treats as a permanent tax.
audit.why: 'Trade when Satchel is down' is unactionable without knowing how long down lasts. These two numbers are the whole rhythm of the lane.
audit.corrected: Rank-1 20 s added to whys[1]; Minefield's flat 16 s added to whys[3].

audit.why: The reactive Satchel hop that dodges Nevermove is already the spine of this page and correctly stated in whys[1], early, and wants.foe[0]. The kit file tags Satchel Charge with a percent-health flag, but Riot's description says only magic damage plus a knock-away — I trusted the description and wrote no percent-health claim.

edits.before: Satchel Charge (W) is a direct counter to Nevermove launch — Ziggs hops out of the root path on reaction, so Level 2 is only marginally better unless you catch him mid-CS animation.
edits.after: Satchel Charge (W) counters Nevermove on reaction — he hops clear of the root path. It is down 20 s at rank 1, so Level 2 only improves once you have seen him spend it.

edits.before: Both champions farm around cooldowns: your E is a kill setup when Satchel is down, Ziggs's Minefield taxes your CS when it is up — neither side decisively owns this window.
edits.after: Both farm around cooldowns: your E is a kill setup when Satchel is down, and Hexplosive Minefield taxes your CS on a flat 16 s — neither side owns this window.

notes: The largest chart correction in my slice: six of seven rows were inverted against their own whys, including a 2+ items row that gave Swain a late game every prose field on the page concedes to Ziggs. All twelve chart edits are proposed as matched win[N]/phases[N].side pairs in one group. Both flagged suspectNames are false positives — 'Satchel Charge' is the correct name. Satchel Charge carries a percent-health derived flag that Riot's description does not support; no percent-health claim was written.
